entries.name: Mastaba tomb
entries.purpose: flat-roofed superstructure over an underground burial shaft; tombs of early kings and officials
parts: battered rectangular slope walls
flat roof
offering chapel and false door
shaft cut to a burial chamber below
layout: a long low bench-like massif, wider than deep
chapel on the east face, shaft descending from the centre
placed in dense necropolis rows at Saqqara and Giza
entries.found: many; hundreds at Saqqara, Giza and Abydos
entries.notes: The ancestor of the pyramid: stacked mastabas became the Step Pyramid. Ideal repeatable desert tomb for an early-period necropolis.

entries.name: Step Pyramid of Djoser
entries.purpose: rock-cut tomb of Pharaoh Djoser, and the first large dressed-stone monument
parts: six mastaba-like steps over a core of rubble
ashlar limestone casing
underground burial chamber and magazines
surrounding stone wall with dummy buildings and courtyards
layout: a stepped stone hill 121 blocks long and 62 blocks tall
north-south oriented, funerary complex several hundred blocks wide to the north and east
open courtyards flank the pyramid inside a high enclosure wall
entries.found: one, at Saqqara northwest of Memphis
entries.notes: Imhotep's design; visible silhouette steps, not the smooth slope of later pyramids. The world's oldest surviving large masonry structure.

entries.name: Valley of the Kings royal tomb (KV62)
entries.purpose: hidden rock-cut burial chambers for New Kingdom pharaohs and nobles
parts: descending corridor sequence
axis turns with burial halls
decorated burial chamber with god and netherworld texts
antechambers and annexes for goods
layout: entrance cut unobtrusively in a cliff face
corridor plunges tens of metres underground
final chamber holds the sarcophagus; over 60 numbered tombs (KV) occupy the wadi
entries.found: one valley of about 63 known tombs, 4 km from Thebes; KV62 (Tutankhamun, 1922) is the most famous
entries.notes: Nothing rises above the desert except a cliff face and stair; the drama is all underground. Model as a carveable cave cut into a wadi.

entries.name: Newgrange passage tomb
entries.purpose: collective megalithic passage tomb; winter solstice sunrise lights the inner chamber
parts: great circular cairn of layered stones
kerb of decorated kerbstones
roofed stone passage 19 m long
three-lobed chamber with corbelled roof
winter solstice roof-box
layout: a near-perfect round grassy mound, 85 blocks across, 13 blocks high
single passage aimed at the winter solstice sunrise
white quartz and granite kerb face on the southeast; satellite mounds nearby
entries.found: one, in the Boyne valley, County Meath
entries.notes: Older than the pyramids and Stonehenge; the only tomb on Earth with a functioning solstice light show. A landmark for a midwinter event.

entries.name: West Kennet Long Barrow
entries.purpose: communal chambered tomb and false-hill landmark
parts: long trapezoidal mound
large terminal sarsen blocking stone
stone-lined burial chambers off a central passage
ditch on each side
layout: a grass ridge 100 blocks long and up to 30 blocks wide, a few blocks high
chambers cluster at the east end; entrance blocked by a great stone
visible from Avebury a few hundred metres south
entries.found: one, on the Wiltshire Downs near Avebury
entries.notes: Exploreable interior on day one; a soft-edged, publicly owned monument, not a ruin. Fits a peaceful prehistory landscape.

entries.name: Treasury of Atreus (tholos tomb)
entries.purpose: beehive-shaped royal (or elite) burial chamber
parts: dromos entrance passage 36 m long
doorway with relieving triangle and half-columns
circular corbelled tholos chamber 14.5 m across
side chamber for goods
layout: a huge grass mound plugged into a hillside
narrow stone-lined forecourt leads to a tall doorway
inside, a perfect corbelled dome rises 13 blocks; decorated ceiling slabs are gone
entries.found: one, at Mycenae
entries.notes: The largest corbelled dome until the Pantheon; robbed in antiquity, so empty but spectacular. A complete interior you can build once and reuse.

entries.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
entries.purpose: tomb of Mausolus, satrap of Caria; the word mausoleum comes from his name
parts: large podium with sculptural friezes
peripteral colonnade of 36 Ionic columns
stepped pyramid 24 tiers high
quadriga chariot statue on the summit
layout: a white marble wedding-cake: rectangular base, colonnade, then a stepped pyramid
friezes ran around every face; pieces are scattered between London and Bodrum
stood beside a great temple-precinct in the satrapal capital
entries.found: one, at Bodrum (Halicarnassus); largely ruined, little but a plinth and a few sculptures survive
entries.notes: One of the Seven Wonders; fewer than ten standing blocks remain, so it is best as a ruin or as a gleaming 'original' showcase.

entries.name: Banditaccia necropolis, Cerveteri
entries.purpose: planned city of the dead mirroring the layout of an Etruscan city
parts: tumulus mounds of laid earth over cut-stone chambers
street grid with rectangular tombs at the edges
carved interiors furnished as houses
grave goods left for the afterlife
layout: broad low hill of round and square mounds laid over a street grid
some streets are wide enough to drive between mounds
400 ha, thousands of tombs, many still with carved chests and rafters
entries.found: one, north of Rome; includes Cucumelletta and Monte Abetone
entries.notes: The best single-site snapshot of an entire Etruscan city of the dead; scale it as a walkable open-air museum of mound tombs.

entries.name: Pyramid of Cestius
entries.purpose: tomb of Gaius Cestius, a Roman praetor; a single-person pyramid in a marble Rome
parts: steep white marble pyramid
interior barrel-vaulted burial chamber with frescoes
inscription naming the owner on both east and west faces
incorporated into the Aurelian Walls
layout: a compact, steep white pyramid wedged between tram lines
smaller than Giza, almost pure silhouette, no complex around it
Porta San Paolo stands at its southwest corner
entries.found: one, in Rome near Testaccio
entries.notes: Proof that Egyptian forms traveled; good as a small, special-case monument. Rare survivor embedded in later fortifications.

entries.name: Castel Sant'Angelo (Mausoleum of Hadrian)
entries.purpose: cylinder mausoleum for Hadrian and later emperors; later a papal fortress and castle
parts: great drum 64 m across on a square podium
spiral internal ramp
topped by a 34 m bronze quadriga (lost)
papal bastions and battlements on top (added 14th-16th c.)
layout: huge round drum faced in travertine, ringed by an earth mound
connected to the Vatican by the fortified Passetto di Borgo
now a layered fortress-castle crowned by a bronze angel
entries.found: one, on the Tiber in Rome
entries.notes: A tomb that grew into a castle; perfect example of a layered landmark where each era adds a story. Original drum height about 21 m.

entries.name: Cahokia Mound 72
entries.purpose: elite burial mound with mass grave of retainers and a shell-bead 'birdman' figure
parts: low low mound 2 m high
buried man arranged on shell-bead cape in bird-like pose
mass grave of c. 53 young women
elite burials with arrowheads of exotic stone
layout: a low oblong earthen mound beside a plaza
alternating layers of ritual fills and burials
one of 120 mounds at the largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico
entries.found: one, in southern Illinois; excavated 1967-71
entries.notes: A small, grim mound that carries the whole mystery of Cahokia's hierarchy; handle human-remains content respectfully in-game.

entries.name: Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa dolmens
entries.purpose: Bronze Age megalithic graves (goindol) and disputed altar stones; Korea holds 40% of the world's dolmens
parts: table-type: upright cist topped by a huge capstone
go-board-type: underground chamber covered by a slab on low supports
some capstones weigh 200-300 t
clusters of 100-500 per hillslope
layout: dozens to hundreds of stone-topped graves dotted over a hillside
largest table stones span 5-7 blocks and rise ~2.5-3 blocks
Korea's west coast hosts ~30,000 of them in total
entries.found: many; three UNESCO clusters (Gochang 447, Hwasun ~500, Ganghwa ~70) plus thousands more nationwide
entries.notes: A whole hillside of identical silhouettes; table-type variants make strong skyline markers. Korea dominates the world dolmen map.

entries.name: Daisen Kofun (tomb of Emperor Nintoku)
entries.purpose: imperial burial mound; largest tomb in the world by ground area
parts: keyhole-shaped mound: round back + triangular front
triple moat system
haniwa terracotta figures lining the terraces
inner burial chamber and stone coffin inside the summit
layout: a perfect keyhole island 486 blocks long, 35 blocks high, surrounded by two or three concentric moats
three distinct precincts: back circle, middle neck, front triangle
part of the Mozu-Furuichi Kofun group, 62 kofun around Osaka
entries.found: one, in Sakai; Imperial Household Agency forbids excavation, contents are unverified
entries.notes: Keyhole shape is unmistakable from the air; do not excavate or furnish interior in-game. Largest tomb on Earth by area.

entries.name: Tomb of Qin Shi Huang (incl. Terracotta Army)
entries.purpose: mausoleum of the First Emperor; a full underground palace with an entire terracotta army guarding it
parts: great rammed-earth pyramid mound
surrounding inner and outer walls
three pits of 8,000 terracotta soldiers, cavalry and chariots
unexcavated inner palace with rivers of mercury according to Sima Qian
layout: a broad grass-covered pyramid hill 350 blocks across, 50 blocks high
army pits lie ~1 km east of the mound
outer necropolis walls enclose 2 km² of still-unexcavated ground
entries.found: one, at Lintong near Xi'an; the army pits opened in 1974
entries.notes: The excavated army is a solved design problem; the sealed inner pyramid stays off-limits and must remain mystery. Largest Chinese imperial tomb.

entries.name: Ming Tombs, Changling (Nanjing's Thirteen Tombs)
entries.purpose: imperial necropolis of 13 Ming emperors; Changling is its largest, the tomb of Yongle
parts: tablet pavilion and Spirit Way with stone guardian animals
Ling'en Hall, a 3-storey 28 m ceremonial hall
tablet mound 'treasure hill'
underground palace excavated at Dingling
layout: a 6 km sacred way winding north through hills into a burial valley
Ling'en Hall faces south with twin flanking towers
13 mounds spread over 40 km² at the foot of Tianshou Shan
entries.found: one complex north of Beijing; Changling best preserved, Dingling excavated 1956-57
entries.notes: The stone-animal procession is an instantly readable landmark sequence; scale the hall to dominate its courtyard.

entries.name: Humayun's Tomb
entries.purpose: mausoleum of Mughal emperor Humayun; prototype of the Taj Mahal
parts: high double-domed central chamber
Persian charbagh garden divided by water channels
octagonal plan on a podium
hundreds of graves of later Mughals inside
layout: a red and white octagonal building standing on a broad square plinth
four-part garden with central pavilion pools
emphasis on bilateral symmetry and a single great dome
entries.found: one, in Delhi; UNESCO World Heritage
entries.notes: Every Mughal tomb after this obeys its grammar; half the size of the Taj but nearly as elegant. Garden is inseparable from the building.

entries.name: Gur-e-Amir (tomb of Timur)
entries.purpose: tomb of Timur (Tamerlane), his sons and grandsons including Ulugh Beg
parts: octagonal base chamber
tall cylindrical drum with huge Kufic script
fluted turquoise dome 15 m across, 64 ribs
jade tombstone of Timur (the nephrite was taken to Mashhad, later split in two)
layout: a single turquoise melon-dome on an octagon, 34 blocks tall
inside, a cruciform chamber lined with onyx and gold
set alone in a walled courtyard off the old citadel
entries.found: one, in Samarkand; opened by Soviets 1941, resealed December 1942
entries.notes: Prototype of every later Timurid and Mughal dome; Timurid empire in one silhouette. Opening the tomb is said to have cursed the USSR.

entries.name: Al-Khazneh (the Treasury at Petra)
entries.purpose: likely a royal Nabataean tomb (not a treasury), possibly Aretas IV
parts: cut straight into the rock face 40 m tall
Corinthian and Nabataean broken pediments
single large chamber inside
siq approach 1.2 km long
layout: one gleaming rose facade framed by the canyon walls
doorway 6 blocks high, facade 40 blocks tall
behind it, a rough square burial chamber cut in the cliff
entries.found: one, at the end of the Siq in Petra; other rock-cut tombs multiply along the roads out of town
entries.notes: The single most photographed facade in the Near East; a tomb that tourists swear hides treasure. Best at dawn from inside the siq.

entries.name: Naqsh-e Rostam royal rock tombs
entries.purpose: cliff-face tombs of Darius I, Xerxes, Artaxerxes and Darius II, plus later Sasanian reliefs
parts: four cruciform facades high above the valley floor
carved 'doors' into solid rock leading to small chambers
colossal royal audience scene above each doorway
Sasanian investiture reliefs below the tombs
layout: four identical cross-shaped carved facades in a cliff 50 m up
face east toward the plain
small square tomb chambers inside each facade, reached by ledges
entries.found: one cliff with four tombs, 12 km northwest of Persepolis
entries.notes: No other place shows Achaemenid and Sasanian glory in the same wall; unreachable without climbing or ladders.

entries.name: Tomb of Cyrus the Great
entries.purpose: simple gabled-roof tomb of Cyrus, founder of the Persian Empire
parts: six stepped receding courses of stone
small house-like chamber
steep gabled roof
no inscription survives; identified by ancient sources
layout: a stark white house on a stepped plinth, 11 blocks high
alone on the plain at Pasargadae
originally wrapped by a walled garden paradise
entries.found: one, at Pasargadae
entries.notes: Deliberately modest; Alexander visited it. A perfect small-scale landmark that reads instantly from the plain.

entries.name: Catacombs of San Callisto
entries.purpose: underground burial galleries of early Christians at Rome
parts: storey upon storey of corridors, up to 20 m deep
loculi wall-burial niches
cubicula painted burial rooms
Popes' crypt
layout: a labyrinth of gallery tunnels running under the Via Appia
visitors walk one way in, another way out
20 km of passage survive in the wider catacomb network
entries.found: one, on the Via Appia Antica, Rome
entries.notes: Atmospheric underground sprawl; darkness, tight 2-block-high passages and named chambers. Keep it eerie, not graphic.

entries.name: Catacombs of Paris (ossuary)
entries.purpose: ossuary holding the exhumed remains of c. 6 million Parisians moved out of overflowing cemeteries
parts: reused Roman and medieval limestone mines
walls lined with carefully stacked skulls and femurs
inscriptions naming the cemeteries of origin
sculptures and altars from the removal campaigns
layout: tunnels 20 m below the Left Bank streets
the open visitor route is ~1.5 km; total quarry area hundreds of km
walls alternate bone facades with black marble plaques
entries.found: one, under the 14th and 5th arrondissements; small open tour route
entries.notes: Carved bone walls make an unforgettable border feature; strictly underground, so no skyline to spoil.

entries.name: Sedlec Ossuary (All Saints, Kutna Hora)
entries.purpose: chapel decorated with the bones of c. 40,000 people, inside All Saints' cemetery church
parts: great central candelabra of bones
bone chandeliers
bone crests and pyramids stacked in the chancel
coat of arms of the Schwarzenberg family in bones
layout: a small vaulted underground chapel, no more than a few blocks wide
bone heaps flank the altar; entrance from the cemetery church above
every flat surface wears bone mosaics
entries.found: one, in Sedlec, Kutna Hora
entries.notes: A true cabinet of curiosities; maximum impact for a single small chamber. Sensitive: keep the tone reverent, not sensational.

entries.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
entries.purpose: Paris municipal cemetery and garden; final resting place of over a million, incl. Chopin, Jim Morrison, Edith Piaf
parts: 110 ha of walled, tree-lined avenues
ornate iron-fenced family vaults
famous single graves (Oscar Wilde's angel, Morrison's plain stone)
cremation columbarium
layout: a walled green hill with a regular Roman grid of streets
avenue graves range from grand temples to plain slabs
permanent, leafy, walk-through city of the dead
entries.found: one, in eastern Paris; ~70,000 plots, ~1 million interments
entries.notes: The archetype of the romantic garden cemetery; good for pilgrimage quests and famous-ghost encounters.

entries.name: Arlington National Cemetery
entries.purpose: military cemetery; over 400,000 veterans and families, including the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
parts: 2.5 km² of white headstone rows
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier with 24-hour sentry
Arlington House overlooking the rows
Section 60 for Iraq/Afghanistan dead
layout: mile after mile of perfectly aligned white markers on a hillside
broad avenues, small woods, and the massive Memorial amphitheatre
visible across the Potomac from Washington
entries.found: one, in Virginia opposite Washington, D.C.; in continuous use since the Civil War
entries.notes: Scale is the point; a repeating headstone field with a few anchor points. Very respectful tone mandatory.

entries.name: Wadi al-Salam Cemetery (Valley of Peace)
entries.purpose: Shi'a cemetery of Najaf; world's largest, with c. 6 million remains, still receiving burials daily
parts: towering multi-storey family mausoleums and crypts
low ground graves
dense urban fabric of tomb architecture without streets of buildings
pilgrimage routes converging on the Imam Ali shrine
layout: a 6+ km² rolling field dense with freestanding tomb towers
walls of crypt doors and paving stones under every block
no orderly grid; sprawl grows outward continuously
entries.found: one, in Najaf; ~600 ha on current estimates, more than 1400 years of accumulation
entries.notes: The biggest city of the dead on Earth; render it as sea of cube-tombs under a hazy desert sky. Working cemetery — not a ruin.

entries.name: Skogskyrkogården (Woodland Cemetery)
entries.purpose: modernist forest cemetery; UNESCO-listed masterwork of 20th-century landscape design
parts: the Woodland Chapel by Asplund
the Hill of Meditation and Cross on the mound
the Resurrection Chapel by Lewerentz
cremation grove integrated in pine forest
layout: granite ridge and pine forest, no perimeter fence
long reflecting pool approach axis to the crematorium
meadow burial fields, intimate small clearings
entries.found: one, in south Stockholm; UNESCO World Heritage 1994
entries.notes: Model landscape over model architecture; the grove is half the message. One of the world's most influential cemetery designs.

entries.name: Lenin's Mausoleum
entries.purpose: tomb of Vladimir Lenin; embalmed body exhibited behind glass
parts: stepped pyramid of five projections
labradorite-faced interior chamber
black band with red smalta zigzags
parade tribune added on the first projection in 1945
layout: a red and black stepped ziggurat pressed against the Kremlin wall
24 blocks wide, 12 blocks high
granite benches for officials run along the side walls
entries.found: one, on Red Square, Moscow
entries.notes: The only major 20th-century tomb built as propaganda; pure silhouette against the wall. Death-cult handling required.

entries.name: Temple I (Temple of the Great Jaguar), Tikal
entries.purpose: funerary pyramid of ruler Jasaw Chan K'awiil I; his tomb sealed inside the base
parts: nine-tiered stepped platform
roof comb crowning the summit shrine
three burial chamber chambers inside the base
stela and altar in the plaza
layout: a 47-block stepped pyramid rising above the rainforest canopy
faces a matching pyramid (Temple II) across the Great Plaza
roof comb is latticed stone openwork, unmistakable against the sky
entries.found: one, at Tikal in the Petén
entries.notes: Americas' answer to Egypt's pyramids; steep staircase and roof comb are essential silhouette cues.

entries.name: Royal Tomb of the Lord of Sipán (Huaca Rajada)
entries.purpose: untouched royal grave of a Moche lord; found with gold, silver, ceramics and three retainers
parts: adobe pyramid (huaca) with burial chamber 2 m below the summit
warrior burial with gold pectorals and earspools
attendant burials of two men and a dog
fine-line stirrup vessels
layout: an eroded adobe platform mound rising from the Lambayeque coastal desert
single deep shaft tomb at its summit
looted 1987, scientifically excavated 1987-89
entries.found: one, near Sipán; remains reburied 1994 as a new museum (Tumbas Reales de Sipán)
entries.notes: The richest single Americas tomb besides the Qin army; often compared to Tutankhamun. Adobe pyramid silhouette, low and worn.

entries.name: Chullpas of Sillustani
entries.purpose: above-ground tower tombs of the Colla and Inca nobility on the shores of Lake Umayo
parts: inverted-cone circular towers
small east-facing opening for the sun's rebirth
stacked family mummies inside
house-sized body niches inside the thick hollow towers
layout: about 90 towers scattered over a headland above a highland lagoon
tallest (the Lagarto) is 12 blocks high and 7 blocks across at the top
fitted Inca ashlar sits among rougher Colla stone
blueprint: legend: s fitted volcanic stone blocks, o small east-facing opening (sealed after the burial), . air
entries.found: one hilltop site, 34 km northwest of Puno, at 3,900 m altitude
entries.notes: Hollow towers visible against the sky; perfectly fits a high-altiplano silhouette question. Door always faces east.

entries.name: Issyk kurgan (Golden Man tomb)
entries.purpose: elite Saka burial; the mound held a teenage warrior buried with 4,000 gold ornaments
parts: round multi-layered mound of pebble and clay
two timber burial chambers inside
gold-plated leather armour and tall headdress
inscribed silver cup (not yet deciphered)
layout: a smooth pebble dome 60 blocks across, 6 blocks high
part of a 45-mound royal cemetery spread over 3 km²
excavated 1969-70 by Akishev
entries.found: one, east of Issyk; the mound is destroyed, its chamber kept intact in a museum
entries.notes: Low honey-coloured dome in endless steppe; unexcavated mounds look like ordinary hillocks with a single tell-tale stone ring.

entries.name: Pazyryk frozen burials (Ukok Plateau)
entries.purpose: elite kurgan burials preserved by permafrost, including the Lady of Ukok with a tattooed arm
parts: stone mound 5-25 m across (royal tumuli up to 60 m)
larch log-cabin chamber under the mound
horses buried with the master
ice-sealed carpets, fabrics, leather, tattoos
layout: small stony mounds in chains running north-south
stones adjusted so water floods the chamber; the water freezes before summer and never thaws
Ukok is 2,200-2,600 m above sea level
entries.found: many, on the Ukok Plateau, Altai; hundreds of sites surveyed
entries.notes: Preserved tattoos, textiles and horses; unsurpassed for showing ancient-animal-style art in a tomb.

entries.name: Tower of Silence (dakhma)
entries.purpose: circular, roofless exposure platform where vultures consume the dead, keeping fire, earth and water unpolluted
parts: squat cylinder 4-6 m high, 15-90 m across
three concentric stone terraces for men, women, children
central bone well (astodan)
inward-sloping floor and drains
layout: a low stone ring on a hilltop, open to the sky
approached by a single gated road through a sacred grove
Yazd's two hilltop towers and Mumbai's five active dakhmas are the iconic survivors
entries.found: one or two per Zoroastrian community; in use at Mumbai, derelict at Yazd since the 1970s
entries.notes: No burial at all: the building is a laying-out platform. Deeply sensitive religious site — model the exterior, never the interior rite.

entries.name: Toraja cliff graves and tau-tau
entries.purpose: cliff-chamber burials of Torajan nobility, marked by life-size wooden effigies (tau-tau)
parts: chambers carved into vertical limestone cliffs
rows of gaudy wooden effigies on ledges
coffins wedged into crevices and caves
lower caves for commoners, cliff tops for nobility
layout: a cliff face studded with niches, some 2-50 m off the ground
effigies stand exposed in rows facing the village
Londa and Lemo are the showpiece sites
entries.found: many, in the Sa'dan highlands of Sulawesi
entries.notes: Face value looks like a balcony of statues; the higher the coffin, the higher the rank. Burial sites are family property, not public art.

entries.name: Hanging coffins (Bo country)
entries.purpose: coffins suspended on high cliff faces by minority peoples of southern China and Sagada in the Philippines
parts: wooden coffins pinned or slotted into cliff ledges
often 30-150 m above the valley floor
weathered coffins slit open by centuries
occasionally on rock outcrops instead of cliffs
layout: coffins strung along sheer limestone faces above rivers
not reachable without ropes or scaffolds
Sagada's Echo Valley and Sichuan's Bo county are the classic sites
entries.found: many, in Sichuan, Yunnan and Guizhou (China) and Sagada (Philippines)
entries.notes: Inexplicable to outsiders without context; villagers say high placement honours the dead. Fragile and irreplaceable — never something to loot.

entries.name: Malagasy family tomb (fasana) and aloalo
entries.purpose: communal stone family tomb; central to the famadihana 'turning of the bones' festival
parts: small house-like stone or brick tomb in the ancestors' field
aloalo wooden carved posts on top
opening on the east for the reburial ceremony
doorway sealed between ritual turns of the dead
layout: a squat stone cottage sitting in a paddy or on an ancestors' hill
laid out in a line with related family tombs
interiors lined with cement and new mats at each turning
entries.found: many, across the central highlands of Madagascar
entries.notes: Living tradition: tombs are tended, opened and whitewashed in the famadihana. Keep the ritual visible and respectful.
